subject.title: Feature request: fallback model chain for compaction and LCM summaryModel

question: Should OpenClaw add a public fallback model chain for explicit embedded compaction models, and should Lossless/LCM `summaryModel` fallbacks be plugin-owned config or a generic context-engine SDK contract?
rationale: The implementation would add public config and provider/auth fallback behavior, and the Lossless half crosses the core/plugin owner boundary; automation should not choose those semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve a scoped core compaction field and plugin-owned Lossless follow-up
options.body: Add a narrow `agents.defaults.compaction.fallbacks` contract for embedded OpenClaw compaction and leave `summaryModel` fallback support to Lossless or a separate plugin-SDK seam decision.

options.title: Design a generic context-engine fallback seam first
options.body: Defer the core config field until maintainers define one SDK-level summary fallback contract that can cover Lossless and other context engines consistently.

options.title: Reject new fallback config and document current behavior
options.body: Keep explicit `compaction.model` exact, rely on session fallbacks only when no explicit compaction model is set, and point Lossless users to plugin-owned configuration.

recommendation.title: Approve a scoped core compaction field and plugin-owned Lossless follow-up
recommendation.body: Add a narrow `agents.defaults.compaction.fallbacks` contract for embedded OpenClaw compaction and leave `summaryModel` fallback support to Lossless or a separate plugin-SDK seam decision.

likelyOwner.reason: The history ties this person to both compaction override docs/tests and the compaction provider registry boundary that this decision would extend.
